cards.front: What should you know about atom?
cards.back: The smallest particle of an element that can still be recognised as that element. Atoms are the building blocks of all matter.

cards.front: What should you know about element?
cards.back: A substance made up of only one type of atom. Each element has a unique atomic number and is listed on the Periodic Table.

cards.front: What should you know about compound?
cards.back: A substance made from two or more elements that are chemically combined in fixed proportions. Compounds can only be separated into their elements by chemical reactions.

cards.front: What should you know about mixture?
cards.back: Two or more substances that are mixed together but are not chemically combined. Mixtures can be separated by physical methods such as filtration, distillation or chromatography.

cards.front: What should you know about chemical symbol?
cards.back: A one- or two-letter abbreviation used to represent an element (e.g. O for oxygen, Na for sodium).

cards.front: What should you know about law of conservation of mass?
cards.back: No atoms are created or destroyed in a chemical reaction, so the number of atoms of each element must be the same on both sides of the equation.

cards.front: What should you know about state symbols?
cards.back: are added to symbol equations to show the physical state of each substance. They are written in brackets after each formula.
One type of atom (e.g. Two or more elements chemically combined)
